# Conditional transfer to the measured scheduled-memory interface

Date: 2026-10-16. Local mathematical audit; no hardware or threshold claim.

## Verdict

A literal replacement of the partial-boundary theorem's ANY-block-mismatch constant by the new one-node endpoint F_K is false. An exact counterexample is below. There are nevertheless two valid conditional improvements:

1. Complete internal syndrome pinchings, including the successful cuts in the old independent latent-pattern refinement: replace the old capped sum of squared block actions by Q = 1 - product_B cos^2(min(a_B, pi/2)), keeping its ANY-block-mismatch predicate.
2. One scalar full-syndrome partial-pinch node: change the parent predicate to entering-versus-final full-syndrome mismatch, retain actual exact entering and final syndrome pinchings, and use F_K on this new CP refinement. The original REPORT support proof extends to this endpoint-based refinement. This changes the certificate, not the physical channel.

Both need the own-entry/retirement embedding described below. The common-initial-time projector theorem alone is not a proof of either full-input scheduled-memory claim.

## A. Exact obstruction to unchanged-event substitution

Use a memory syndrome qubit with stabilizer Z and an untouched logical spectator. The weak footprint is the syndrome qubit, so its commuting Paulis are I and Z and the full-footprint/no-local-logical condition holds. Enter in |0>, apply U=exp(-i pi X/6), then T=(Id+D_Z)/2, then U, and perform the actual final Z pinching. Correction is identity. All resources may be reserved in one clean parent.

The stipulated channel has its old canonical independent skip/complete-pinch refinement. On a retained middle pinch, the event of at least one block mismatch has probability 1-(3/4)^2=7/16. On a skipped middle pinch, the sole block mismatch probability is sin^2(pi/3)=3/4. Thus the OLD parent event has probability 19/32.

The new binary endpoint formula gives F_1(pi/6,pi/6,1/2)=9/16=18/32. Indeed the actual endpoint mismatch probability is (1/2)(2(1/4)(3/4))+(1/2)(3/4)=18/32. The omitted 1/32 consists of retained-pinch paths that leave and return to the entering syndrome. They are bad in the old event and good in the new endpoint event. Consequently F_1 cannot bound the old event even for a single parent and trivial bath.

This is not a controller, geometry, or logical-e

# Retained cuts with per-segment propagated error kernels

16 October 2026. New local extension of the supplied support argument, proved here. No new physical boundary is inserted. This is a sufficient algebraic and causal theorem, not a lifetime theorem or a hardware qualification.

## 1. Typed contract

Let S be a commuting Pauli stabilizer code group with no -I, encoding isometry V:L->M, and a persistent finite bath B. A reference R and arbitrary initial L-B-R entanglement are permitted. The probability/effect statement below is stronger in its input domain: it allows arbitrary physical M-B-R inputs.

Fix an exogenous finite schedule. Each clean parent is bounded by its genuine entering instrument/correction and actual completion instrument. Refine its weak part by **actual** intermediate complete syndrome cuts. For segment c, denote its entering/exiting projectors by P_(c,r),P_(c,t) for a commuting G_c subset S. Same-G neighboring segments may share a single actual cut and its classical/latent label. A different G requires the actual corresponding instrument, not a retrospective change of labels. Trusted intended Pauli correction occurs at its actual prescribed start; it is not moved through the weak interval.

An unread cut is allowed only when the complete full-joint channel is the stipulated pinching, with fresh isolated discarded environment and no future use/return. Its canonical environment labels are complete actual-channel Kraus labels. They need not be controller readouts. 16 October 2026. Exact local algebra and model-scoped receiving analysis. No native-memory no-go theorem is claimed.

## 1. Model identity

The current N881 dossier and the GD reconstruction distinguish:

| Model | Actual quantum operation | Admitted noise in the reconstructed theorem |
|---|---|---|
| Original active pair | kappa sum D[Q Pi] | Declared continual independent face Pauli noise |
| Completed pair | kappa sum (C-Id), C(X)=Q Pi X Pi Q^dagger+(I-Pi)X(I-Pi) | Rare bounded-patch CPTP proposal faults with input-independent fixed location rates, plus separately proved supported compilers/floors |
| Whole-vertex/depolarized completion | Different aggregated completion and physical full-patch floors | Its own regularized perturbation contract and larger supports |
| Measured scheduled protection | Trusted actual entering sector/correction, weak interval with stipulated nodes, actual full-G completion pinching, full clean reservation | Its stated weak/Schur channel contract; robust local slot errors only with the additional full-joint and propagated-support premises |

The first three are not identified with the fourth. The assigned W pin is f937563cbc5d2249b8e0dd96bcbd3b8f78eb85c6. This investigation read files at W without running Git or modifying that checkout.

For the pair, Pi=(I-S_1)(I-S_2)/4. Completed minus active generator is exactly kappa D[I-Pi]. It vanishes on definite-syndrome Pauli density operators, but generally acts on syndrome coherences. Thus even completion is a physical model change for coherent inputs.

## 2. Native pair records do not supply full syndrome cuts

because Pi annihilates both vectors and I-Pi acts identically. Therefore
